sections.heading: Fix What's Broken, Tell You the Truth
body: The air quits in the hottest week of July, or the furnace on the first cold night. Someone comes out, takes a quick look and says you need a whole new system. You're hot or cold, tired, and in no shape to argue.

That's when it matters who shows up. Preston has been in the HVAC industry since 1999 and Justin since 2000, and the way we work comes from those years: find the actual problem, explain it in plain words, and fix that.
We guarantee 100% satisfaction with all our work. We'd rather earn the next call than sell you more than you need.

That's why you'll get a straight answer: a repair when a repair will do, and a new system only when it's the better choice. Often the fix is smaller than you feared, like a filter and a setting nobody checked.

sections.heading: AC Repair
body: Warm air from the vents, a unit that runs all afternoon and never catches up, an outdoor fan that won't start. Those are the usual signs of a system that has lost a part or lost its charge.

Most of the time it's something small: a capacitor that has worn out, a coil caked with dirt, a refrigerant leak, or a thermostat that has stopped talking to the unit. Finding which one takes a technician who has seen it before.
We work on all makes and models. We diagnose the problem, show you what we found and fix it. If the unit is beyond saving, we'll tell you that too, and why.

sections.heading: Furnace Repair
body: A house that won't warm up, a furnace that clicks and never lights, a blower that rattles or a smell you can't place. In a Kansas winter, none of that can wait.
Furnaces fail for a short list of reasons: an ignition part that has worn out, a clogged filter, a blower motor, a thermostat problem. Most are fixable, and the repair is worth making.
Some furnaces are at the end of their life, and we'll say so plainly. When that's the case, we'll show you what's worn out, so the decision is about the furnace in front of you, not a sales pitch.

A new high-efficiency system costs less to run, filters the air better and holds humidity down in a Wichita summer. We install complete systems, furnace and AC together or one at a time.
Before you decide, you get the options and what each one means for your house. The choice stays with you.

We repair and replace geothermal and water-source heat pump systems, and mini split systems as well.

sections.heading: Signs Your AC Needs Repair
body: The house won't get below 80 even though the unit is running. The vents blow warm air.
The outdoor fan sits still, or the unit starts, stops and starts again. Ice shows up on the lines, or water pools around the indoor unit.
Each of those points to a specific failure, and some of them get worse every hour the unit keeps running. If you see ice, turn the system off and call us.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: Air conditioners work hard in a Wichita summer, and the same few parts wear out first.
A capacitor helps the compressor and fan motor start, and when it weakens the outdoor unit hums and does nothing. A dirty condenser coil can't shed heat, so the system runs long and cools poorly.
Low refrigerant means a leak somewhere, because an air conditioner doesn't use it up. And a restricted filter or a failed thermostat can make a healthy system look broken.
Telling these apart takes testing, not guessing. Our technicians check the system, find the failure and then tell you what it is.

sections.heading: You'll See What We Found
body: Most people have never looked inside their outdoor unit, and they shouldn't have to. But a bill for a part you never saw is hard to trust.
So we start with the problem you called about. The technician looks at the system, shows you what's wrong and what it takes to fix it, and then does the repair.
We work on all makes and models, so you don't need to know who made your unit. Tell us what it's doing and we'll take it from there.

A repair call should end with a repaired air conditioner. We fix what's broken, and we suggest more only when it will actually help you.
If your system has a bad part and plenty of life left, that's a repair. We'd rather you call us again next summer because we got it right than because we sold you something you didn't need.

When that's the case, we tell you straight and lay out your options. We install complete high-efficiency air conditioning and furnace systems, so you can replace the AC alone or both together.
You may find out it's a repair, and you may find out it's time for a new unit. Either way, you'll know before you decide.

sections.heading: When a Furnace Needs a Technician
body: The house won't warm up. The furnace clicks and never lights, or it lights and shuts off a minute later.
The blower rattles, squeals or never starts. You smell something burning that isn't a candle.
Don't keep restarting a furnace that shuts itself off. It's shutting off for a reason, and the reason is easier to fix before you've run it ten more times.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: Furnaces start the same way every cycle, so the parts that do the starting wear out first.
An igniter or flame sensor that has gone bad is a common reason a furnace clicks and quits. A clogged filter chokes airflow, and the furnace overheats and shuts down to protect itself.
A blower motor can wear out, and a thermostat problem can leave a healthy furnace never getting the call to run.
Each of these is a different repair with a different cost. We find the real one before we start.

sections.heading: A Word on Safety
body: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility from outside before you call anyone else. If a carbon monoxide alarm goes off, get everyone out and call 911.
A furnace that makes a burning smell or soot around the vents also needs to be shut off until a technician has looked at it.

body: The furnace is old, it just quit, and you're wondering whether to sink more money into it. Plenty of furnaces run for decades, so age alone isn't a reason to replace one.
A furnace that needs a cheap part and runs fine is a repair.

A furnace with a cracked heat exchanger, one that needs repair after repair or can't keep the house warm is a different case. We'll tell you which one you have, and we won't hurry you into the expensive one.

We'll go over your options with you and keep the schedule moving, because a house with no heat is not a project you want to stretch out.
